a temporary attribute boost that is not wholly applied lowers the attribute for good: the boost is cut only by the excess over the maximum and then recorded in full, but AddAttribute keeps the attribute within 1..99 and under the maximum plus the largest single boost (R029+0x4E0C); the expiry takes back the recorded amount, so a boost cut short (an attribute near 99, or a second boost overlapping a larger one, in either order) leaves the attribute lower than before. the weapon potions add to the bonus byte without a limit and their bonus event (0x4A) is never undone (EventExpiry.UndoBoost): they last for good and stack, and the nibbles wrap (Deadly Blade's damage nibble loses its carry out of the byte, so a fourth potion can leave +1; Strongedge's carries into the damage nibble).
Strongedge and Great Power record the pack index as the bonus event's type (Deadly Blade records the potion code).

Great Power adds 14/22/30 to the whole damage-and-penetration byte (+14 penetration; +1 damage +6; +1 damage +14, with the carries), where the manual has it raise the weapon's quality by that much, up to 99.

Hardarmor and Firewall never wear off: they raise the armour byte (+0x41) and the Firewall strength (+0x10, below) with no event, and nothing lowers them again (the manual gives them a day); the armour nibble carries past 15 into the fire-charm bits, which Attacks.HitDamage also counts as armour.
v - fame is stored (FixFameCost).

the helps of the two Pauls are mixed up: St.Paul gets R039+0x7C6A, whose feast day (66) and help are those DARKLAND.SNT gives St.Paul the Simple; St.Paul the Simple (106) gets R039+0x7D0C, a copy of St.Thomas Aquinas's help (R039+0x8B58); the help described for St.Paul is R039+0x9578, which no saint number reaches (Z-9318d7).
the saints' charms never wear off: FirewallForAll, like SetCharm and AddCharm, sets the charm byte (+0x41) and its strength (+0x10) with no event, and nothing takes them back.

St.Theodore Tiro raises Flail Weapons twice for a flail wielder: WeaponSkills already raises it for a member holding a flail, and the saint then raises it again; his help also does not match DARKLAND.SNT (all weapon skills, Charisma, Riding): no Riding, Endurance instead.
"learn the saint of this place" (R056 19c4) and the teaching saints pass -1 and teach nobody (FixSaintLearnedByLeader).
the count has no limit: the 256th item of one kind makes it 0, and the stored items are lost.

the original compares its uninitialised size slot where cur_loc was meant (checked against asm 1D72: mov dx,[bp-2]; cmp dx,5Ch; inc dx); OriginalBehaviour.FixShopStockSize uses the city size always.

buying into a full pack loses the money: the price is paid before the item is added and the screen does not test the pack, so with 64 stacks and none that the item joins, AddStack adds nothing and the money is not given back.

by day, trouble on the way to the grove still leads back to the night grove: after the hour has passed the encounter always returns to card 0x22 (named OtherGateAtNight here), while the clear way and the day side street choose 0x21/0x22 by daylight.
the arrival finds the best climber with a local maximum but never stores his value, so the grapple option's chance is a stale value from the last time everybody climbed (0 at first).
compares each member with DS:582A instead of the running minimum.

the pop-up handler returns -1 as the "chance", and the draw (0..99) is never at most -1: the potion always fails (and, as twice the chance is below the draw, the party then goes to card 1).
gossip at the second house shows text 2 twice: there is no else, so text 2 comes again after texts 2 and 12, as in the original.
the pop-up handler returns -1 as the "chance", and the draw (0..99) is never at most -1: the potion always fails, the success branch below never runs.

the hint shows R136+0x8690+0x1E5F ("You need a missile weapon") where "Not enough money" was surely meant.

the two stable texts look swapped: a party all of whose present members have a mount gets text 1, and any other party text 7, the only one in which the stablemaster asks whether the party's mounts are for sale (R051+0x0EE0).

the errand is made for giver 0, the town's merchants, where the card's own tests (an errand open, one done: option 8) look for 3, the bishop: the merchants pay for it and the canon gives a new errand at every visit.

confession can take no time or negative time: standing / -10 + 11 hours is 0 at standing 110..119 and negative from 120 (reachable: a quest's resolution adds standing without a limit, R029+0x3E06); PassHours then turns the clock back, and the hour can become negative (R057+0x03CC).

a second fight at the gate does not lower the standing further: the standing is the one read when the card was entered (R058+0x0E24), and after a fight that keeps the party at the gate the menu runs again with it, so the second fight sets it to that value - 40 again (R058+0x17DA).
the line that is closed for lack of money is 1 ("abandon the horses and crawl out through a sewer"), not the bribe line 2; kept as in the original.
only formulas 0..21 are ever for sale: the offer is taken modulo 22 (the number of potions) but used as a formula number (potion = n / 3, grade = n % 3), so only the first eight potions are offered.
woken at night, the bowyers sell the smiths' goods: the night shop passes the smiths' categories (0xFF, 0x400) where the day shop passes the bowyers' (0x30, 0x83C).

the search tests formulas_known[m][n / 3] && 1 << n % 3 (logical, not bitwise): it skips any n whose group of three has any formula known, not just n itself. If all groups do, the first n is learnt.
debt notes name their holder by +0x2A % 2 (Medici, Fugger), but MerchantHouseOffices finds them in office +0x2A % 4, so the named office is often not the one that holds them.
the offer's option lines are never switched on (R128+0x0806 cleared opt_on[] and the menu loop that copies the flags has not run yet), so the box offers nothing to choose.

the formula's risk works backwards: the explosion (longer = 1, the inn barred 120 days) comes when rand_mod(4 - risk) is not 0, so a low-risk formula (0) explodes three times in four and a high-risk one (2) half the time.
boosts given to the whole party are never taken back (FixEverybodyBoostsUndone).

the weapon potions' kind 0x4A events (Deadly Blade, Strongedge, Great Power: PotionEffects.Drink) run out here and nothing is undone: only kinds 0x48 and 0x49 are, so the bonus byte (+0x34) keeps them for good.

the recorded amount is taken off whatever the attribute is by then (add_attr(owner, type, -value)): a boost that a night's rest (Endurance back to its maximum) or wounds (Strength) have already used up is taken off again and leaves the attribute below where it was; a saint's lowering (a negative value) is given back the same way.

"forever" events end on 31 December 1499: 9999 hours is the fixed end 23:00 31.12.1499, not an open end, so on 1 January 1500 every such event expires (a quest clears its facts) and one created later expires at the next expiry pass; the witches' sabbat quest and its planned sabbat end for good.
the new event already holds the value before the op (FixNewEventAddDoubles).

the whole charm byte but bit 7 counts as armour: its high nibble (bits 4-6) is the fire charm that Firewall (+1 each), St.Polycarp, St.Charity and the other SetCharm saints set, so they give +16 to +112 armour that never wears off (the "invulnerable after Polycarp and Firewall" bug); only the low nibble is the potions' and saints' armour.

the weapon potions' bonus byte counts with any weapon the member strikes with (bows and fists too), where the manual and the potions' own descriptions limit Deadly Blade, Strongedge and Great Power to some kinds of weapon.
the penetration wraps: (bonus + weapon) & 15, so Strongedge or Great Power on a weapon of high penetration gives almost none ("after Great Power my bows only do 3-5 damage").
the original removes an empty group by shifting the later groups down but keeps testing the same (stale, zero) counter, so every group after the first empty one is removed too.

the original draws until the room differs from the gate room, which never happens when the only room it can draw is the gate room (the game then freezes; the emulated original does not return for seed 49955, lore 3, cleared 28, specs (46,4,2) (60,6,8) (41,5,3)).

a corridor's decoration spot can fall past its end: it is counted from the far end (o1, and o3 below) rather than from o0 (o2), so only a roll of 1 falls on the corridor; larger rolls test, and may mark, the cells past its end.
the fortress relics are forced to quality 35: the three relics get quality 0x23 and type 0x9F whatever DARKLAND.LST gives them (the relic weapons have qualities 50..85 and weapon types).
loot counts wrap at 255: the counts are added in a byte with no limit test, so equal items totalling more than 255 wrap and the excess is lost.
items are consumed until none of that type and quality is left: the spares stacked with the worn piece (worn down with it by WearItem) are thrown away with it.
armour wear hits the whole stack: the stack loses the quality, not one piece, so identical spare pieces stacked with the worn armour wear down with it.
the loop runs to the count inclusive, so the slot after the last cloud (an old cloud's copy, or zeros) is tested too (OriginalBehaviour.FixCloudLineOneTooMany stops at the last cloud).
a missed box reloads the line from the saved words, which are the stack residue until a box was hit: the clouds after it are tested against that line (3, 17405)-(state words), not a → t. Kept.

DS:9084 (Battle.LeaveAfterVictory, set when an enemy that ends the battle dies) is not among what is written (R003 never touches it): a castle battle saved after its lord fell and loaded again does not end with the victory, and leaving counts as fleeing.
